⚠️🌏 July–August Flood Risk Outlook | #Asia #China 

Based on composite anomaly signals, a broad belt of above-normal rainfall is evident across East, South, and Southeast Asia.

 Deep green shading indicates persistent rainfall episodes with elevated runoff and flood risk.

Countries and key regions at risk:
China: Central, Eastern, and Southern China — including the Yangtze basin, Sichuan Basin, and coastal provinces

India: Northeast and Eastern India — Assam, Meghalaya, West Bengal, and Himalayan foothills

Bangladesh: Nationwide — especially the Ganges–Brahmaputra delta

Nepal & Bhutan: Southern slopes and foothills (high runoff potential)

Myanmar: Northern, central, and coastal regions
Thailand: Northern and central plains

Laos: Northern and central regions

Vietnam: Northern Vietnam and central highlands/coastal belt

Cambodia: Mekong basin and Tonlé Sap region
Philippines: Parts of Luzon and central islands (episodic heavy rainfall risk)

Taiwan: Island-wide elevated rainfall signal
South Korea: Central and southern regions
Japan: Western and southern regions (including Kyushu and Shikoku).

SE and S China stands out for high risk of floods between June-August and Japan south risk capitalized in September.  

💧 The spatial pattern suggests recurrent rainfall waves rather than isolated events, increasing the likelihood of: Riverine flooding Flash floods
Saturated soils and landslides.

This is a probabilistic, analog-based summer signal, but the consistency across regions points to a notable hydrological risk window during the July–August 2026 transition .
